<thought>The spectrum shows a clear M+1 peak (184.048) at ~10% of the base, matching the characteristic 13C isotopic pattern, indicating carbon is present. It also shows a prominent M+2 peak (185.042) at ~33% of the base, which aligns with the typical chlorine isotopic distribution (35Cl/37Cl ≈ 3:1). No other distinctive isotopic patterns (e.g., bromine’s 1:1 M+2, sulfur’s low‑abundance M+2) are evident. Therefore, carbon and chlorine can be definitively identified.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl']</final_answer>
